task_text: Moving bank relay: A low-friction puck is already sliding toward the right arm at the start, through the first of two gaps in a row of posts across the table. The right Panda's paddle must strike it back toward the left. The puck must then come back through that same gap, hit a small bank board that slides back and forth by itself on the left arm's side of the posts, while the board is moving, and then hit the left Panda's paddle. The right paddle strikes the puck back a second time. The puck must then come back through the second gap and hit the left paddle again, with the paddle at a clearly different position and angle from the first rebound. Finally the left paddle must send the same puck back out through the second gap and across a goal line in front of a backstop wall on the right arm's side, with the right paddle not touching it after it passes the gap. Phases, in order: right_first_strike: The right paddle strikes the puck back toward the left arm. The phase completes at a step within 0.05 s after the puck's last contact with the right paddle at which the puck touches neither paddle, its centre is at world x > 0.18 (on the right arm's side of the posts) and its velocity along x is -0.20 m/s or less (moving toward the left arm at 0.20 m/s or more).; left_first_rebound: The puck's centre crosses the line x = 0.16 moving in -x with |y - (-0.01)| < 0.048 m, i.e. back through gap 0 (x >= 0.16 on the previous physics step and < 0.16 now). After that crossing it hits the bank board while the board slides at 0.02 m/s or more (its joint speed on the previous physics step), and after that bank contact it hits the left paddle while approaching at 0.08 m/s or more (the puck's horizontal speed on the previous physics step). The phase completes at that left-paddle contact, and the left paddle's tool-frame pose (position and orientation) is recorded. A right-paddle contact at any point, or a left-paddle contact before the bank contact, cancels the crossing: a new crossing of gap 0 is then needed. A bank contact while the board is slower does not count, and neither does a left-paddle contact after the bank contact at a lower approach speed; neither cancels anything.; right_recovery_strike: As right_first_strike: the right paddle strikes the puck back toward the left arm (within 0.05 s after its last right-paddle contact, which must be made during this phase, the puck touches neither paddle, is at x > 0.18 and moves at -0.20 m/s or less along x), at a step more than 0.06 s after this phase began.; left_changed_rebound: During this phase the puck's centre crosses x = 0.16 moving in -x with |y - 0.16| < 0.048 m, i.e. through gap 1. After that crossing the puck hits the left paddle while approaching at 0.08 m/s or more, with two pose conditions holding: the paddle's tool-frame origin is more than 0.035 m from the recorded first-rebound position, and its orientation is rotated by more than 0.24 rad (about 13.8 deg) from the recorded orientation, i.e. |q . q_first| < cos 0.12. A right-paddle contact cancels the crossing. Left contacts that do not meet the speed or pose conditions do not count, but they neither cancel the crossing nor fail the task. The bank board plays no part in this phase.; terminal_goal: The puck's centre crosses x = 0.16 moving in +x with |y - 0.16| < 0.048 m, i.e. out through gap 1; a right-paddle contact after that crossing cancels it. The phase completes when, after such a crossing, the puck's centre crosses x = 0.42 moving in +x with |y - 0.16| < 0.055 m while it does not touch the right paddle, and the left paddle has touched the puck at some step after this phase began. This completes the task. Goal geometry: Crossing lines for the puck's centre. Gap 0 line: x = 0.16 with |y + 0.01| < 0.048 m, crossed in -x (left_first_rebound). Gap 1 line: x = 0.16 with |y - 0.16| < 0.048 m, crossed in -x (left_changed_rebound) and in +x (terminal_goal). Strike release: puck centre at x > 0.18. Goal line: x = 0.42 with |y - 0.16| < 0.055 m, crossed in +x.
episode: one episode, no reset: it ends at the first control step where the task has succeeded (every phase in order) or failed (a failure event, a forbidden contact, a safety-limit violation, an object out of bounds, or the task's horizon of 25 s of simulated time, 2500 control steps), when your time is up, or on a simulator error; the simulated clock advances only with the control steps you run
